conditions.name: Drug-Induced Parkinsonism
reviewNotes: Pending manual review of 38 CFR rating codes. Added 2026-09-28 as a versioned catalog addition (814/814 to 817/817) closing the missing-identity gap behind the batch-88 psychotropic-medication-damage neurological withholding, which withheld the neurological half of that request in full because the catalog carried no identity for tardive dyskinesia, drug-induced parkinsonism, neuroleptic malignant syndrome or serotonin syndrome. Reserved evidence pointer: PMID 30695288 (French FACE-SZ cohort of 674 community-dwelling patients with schizophrenia; 13.2 percent drug-induced parkinsonism by Simpson-Angus scale; first-generation antipsychotic prescription adjusted odds ratio 2.038, p = 0.047) is reserved with the held batch-90 schizophrenia route, and any reuse must be adjudicated together with docs/batch-90-schizophrenia-tardive-dyskinesia-held-edge.json under the ME-29 reserved-evidence discipline.

Rating authority is deliberately left empty per docs/condition-catalog.md step 4 (never invent a code): a qualified human must confirm the applicable diagnostic code and framework before any ratingSchedule citation is recorded, and any citation added by automated work stays verified: false. A drug-induced movement disorder is most likely evaluated under the neurological ratings schedule (38 CFR 4.124a), including any analogous rating, but no code and no schedule assignment is asserted here.

Scope guards: this identity is the ACUTE REVERSIBLE drug-induced parkinsonism (a dopamine-blocking drug effect with a distinct natural history), NOT the neurodegenerative disease of the sibling parkinsons-disease identity; per the batch-88 category-error guard, the Piedmont degenerative-parkinsonism hazard-ratio literature (PMID 34652577, HR 3.27 on 2,526,319 residents) studies a different outcome and must not be registered in either direction. Tardive dyskinesia, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and serotonin syndrome are separate identities and must not be routed through this one; dystonia and akathisia remain missing identities and must not be routed through this one either. Bare 'parkinsonism' and the abbreviation 'DIP' are deliberately NOT aliases: 'parkinsonism' is ambiguous against idiopathic and atypical parkinsonian syndromes, and 'DIP' against distal interphalangeal and other expansions.

conditions.name: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
reviewNotes: Pending manual review of 38 CFR rating codes. Added 2026-09-28 as a versioned catalog addition (814/814 to 817/817) closing the missing-identity gap behind the batch-88 psychotropic-medication-damage neurological withholding. EVIDENCE-TIER GATE STANDS: the located literature for this syndrome is dominated by case reports and post-marketing signal analyses, and batch 88 recorded that a non-case-report anchor tier is required even once the identity exists, so no route may be authored to this identity until a cohort, trial or systematic-review anchor is located and verified under docs/citation-verification-sop.md.

Scope guards: this identity is the dopamine-antagonist (neuroleptic/antipsychotic) toxidrome, distinct from the serotonergic toxidrome of the sibling serotonin-syndrome identity and from catatonia; the two toxidromes must not be conflated or routed through each other. Tardive dyskinesia, drug-induced parkinsonism and serotonin syndrome are separate identities; dystonia and akathisia remain missing identities and must not be routed through this one. The abbreviation 'NMS' is deliberately NOT an alias, matching the abbreviation discipline of the tardive-dyskinesia entry.

conditions.name: Tardive Dyskinesia
reviewNotes: Pending manual review of 38 CFR rating codes. Added 2026-09-28 as a versioned catalog addition closing the missing-identity gap behind the batch-80 evidence-preserving refusal of schizophrenia to tardive-dyskinesia (TENTH refusal; authoring-quality evidence preserved at PMID 37424417, PMID 39240484, PMID 42030922) and behind the batch-88 psychotropic-medication-damage neurological withholding (PMID 28146614 and PMID 30695288 reserved).

Rating authority is deliberately left empty per docs/condition-catalog.md step 4 (never invent a code): a qualified human must confirm the applicable diagnostic code and framework before any ratingSchedule citation is recorded, and any citation added by automated work stays verified: false. A movement disorder is most likely evaluated under the neurological ratings schedule (38 CFR 4.124a), including any analogous rating, but no code and no schedule assignment is asserted here.

Scope guards: this identity is the chronic DRUG-INDUCED movement disorder (tardive dyskinesia, most commonly antipsychotic or neuroleptic induced), NOT the neurodegenerative parkinsonism of the sibling parkinsons-disease identity, and the Piedmont degenerative-parkinsonism hazard-ratio literature (PMID 34652577) stays reserved and category-guarded in the batch-88 disposition. Drug-induced parkinsonism, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and serotonin syndrome remain separate missing identities and must not be routed through this one. Bare 'dyskinesia' and the abbreviation 'TD' are deliberately NOT aliases: 'dyskinesia' is ambiguous against primary ciliary dyskinesia and acute extrapyramidal syndromes, and 'TD' against traveler's diarrhea.

Update 2026-09-28 (same-day movement-disorder migration): drug-induced parkinsonism, neuroleptic malignant syndrome and serotonin syndrome were added as separate catalog identities in the versioned 814/814 to 817/817 migration, so the statement above that they 'remain separate missing identities' is superseded as to IDENTITY EXISTENCE only; the prohibition on routing those syndromes through this identity stands unchanged, and dystonia and akathisia remain missing identities.
